# Command reference

Every command prints its result as JSON on stdout and its progress on stderr, so scripts and agents can read the result directly. Running `tripshots` with no arguments opens [the app](app.md).

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`make`](#make) | build a reel from folders/files of photos and clips |
| [`clone`](#clone) | remake a reel you like shot for shot with your own footage |
| [`render`](#render) | re-render an (edited) plan.json |
| [`export`](#export) | hand the edit to Resolve / Premiere / Final Cut: EDL, OTIO, storyboard.md |
| [`learn`](#learn) | learn a style from reference reels (URLs or files) |
| [`music`](#music) | download the sound of an Instagram reel (or any yt-dlp link) |
| [`scan`](#scan) | analyze + score footage and list the best shots |
| [`frame`](#frame) | pop-out frame stills: the subject steps out of a framed photo |
| [`look`](#look) | copy the colour grade of reels/videos/photos you like into a reusable look |
| [`looks`](#looks) | list colour looks (built-in and yours) |
| [`grade`](#grade) | colour grade photos and videos (graded copies + before/after sheet) |
| [`sounds`](#sounds) | sound effects: what's available per role, or --fetch real ones from Openverse |
| [`listen`](#listen) | earshot listens to a finished reel: events, sync, loudness (optional models) |
| [`maps`](#maps) | route-map layer (HyperFrames): status, or --setup to install it |
| [`library`](#library) | what TripShots remembers about your footage (and clearing it) |
| [`styles`](#styles) | list styles |
| [`ui`](#ui) | open the interactive app (same as running tripshots with no arguments) |
| [`find`](#find) | find footage by place, people and dates; saves a selection for `make sel:<id>` |
| [`trips`](#trips) | your footage grouped into trips (dates, places, counts) |
| [`footage`](#footage) | show or set the folders `find` and agents search by default |
| [`people`](#people) | recognise people in your footage (on this computer): add me / discover / name |
| [`edits`](#edits) | finish a reel in Instagram's Edits app (Mac): package / tools / probe / push |
| [`ask`](#ask) | plain language: tripshots ask "a reel about my days in Yellowstone" |
| [`mcp`](#mcp) | run as an MCP server for AI agents (Claude Desktop/Code, OpenClaw, ...) |
| [`doctor`](#doctor) | check dependencies |

## make

```text
usage: tripshots make [-h] [-m MUSIC]
                      [--text-preset {bold,editorial,minimal,handwritten,typewriter}]
                      [--behind {auto,on,off}] [--split-screens {lots,some,off}]
                      [--speed-ramps {on,off}] [--labels {ai,off}] [--loop | --no-loop]
                      [--min-score N] [--look LOOK] [--grade-strength 0-1] [--variants N]
                      [--route-map {intro,tracker,both,off}] [--allow-similar] [--music-start SEC]
                      [--upload-copy | --no-upload-copy] [--cookies-from-browser BROWSER]
                      [--cookies FILE] [--sfx {on,off}] [--ambience {on,off}]
                      [--clip-sound {auto,on,off}] [--sfx-level DB] [--sfx-licenses LIST]
                      [-s STYLE] [-d DURATION] [-o OUT] [-b BACKEND] [--hook HOOK]
                      [--location LOCATION] [--no-location] [--dry-run] [-j WORKERS]
                      [--exclude GLOB] [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--until YYYY-MM-DD] [--no-recursive]
                      [--include-live-photos] [--watch {auto,gemini,off}] [--rescore]
                      [--encoder {auto,hardware,software,videotoolbox,nvenc,qsv}]
                      inputs [inputs ...]

positional arguments:
  inputs                folders and/or files, sel:<id> from `tripshots find`, or @list.txt with
                        one path per line

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -m, --music MUSIC     audio file to cut to (mp3/m4a/wav), or an Instagram reel link to use its
                        sound
  --text-preset {bold,editorial,minimal,handwritten,typewriter}
                        text look (overrides the style)
  --behind {auto,on,off}
                        location title behind the skyline
  --split-screens {lots,some,off}
                        split-screen / grid moments
  --speed-ramps {on,off}
                        velocity speed ramps on moving clips
  --labels {ai,off}     a short AI label on each shot
  --loop, --no-loop     seamless loop ending
  --min-score N         lowest AI score (1-10) a shot may have to be used (default: style's
                        min_score - 2)
  --look LOOK           colour grade: auto (AI picks), none, a preset (see `tripshots looks`) or a
                        look you made with `tripshots look`
  --grade-strength 0-1  how strongly the look is applied (default 0.75)
  --variants N          make N versions (different opening shot, order, transitions and hook) + a
                        comparison sheet, e.g. to test with Instagram trial reels
  --route-map {intro,tracker,both,off}
                        animated travel-route map from your GPS: intro = big card early on,
                        tracker = small corner map following each shot (needs Node.js; first use
                        installs HyperFrames)
  --allow-similar       also use shots the AI flagged as near-duplicates (bursts, same view)
  --music-start SEC     start the song here (default: best part of a file; 0:00 for a reel link)
  --upload-copy, --no-upload-copy
                        also write an upload copy without the music (NAME.nomusic.mp4, which keeps
                        the sound effects; NAME.noaudio.mp4 without sound design), then add the
                        sound in Instagram (default: on when --music is a link)
  -s, --style STYLE     style name or path to YAML
  -d, --duration DURATION
                        target length in seconds
  -o, --out OUT         output .mp4 path
  -b, --backend BACKEND
                        claude-cli | api | minimax | none (default: auto)
  --hook HOOK           on-screen hook text (overrides style/AI)
  --location LOCATION   location label text (overrides GPS lookup)
  --no-location         no location label
  --dry-run             write plan + storyboard only
  -j, --workers WORKERS
  --encoder {auto,hardware,software,videotoolbox,nvenc,qsv}
                        video encoder: auto (default: the Mac's / GPU's hardware encoder when it
                        works, else libx264), hardware, software (libx264, slowest, smallest
                        files), or a specific one

instagram login (most reels need it):
  --cookies-from-browser BROWSER
                        chrome | safari | firefox | brave | edge (use the browser where you're
                        logged in to Instagram; 'chrome:Profile 1' for another profile). Default:
                        $TRIPSHOTS_COOKIES_BROWSER
  --cookies FILE        cookies.txt exported from your browser (alternative)

sound design (real sound effects on the cuts, ambience per place):
  --sfx {on,off}        sound effects on transitions, the drop, text pops (default: style)
  --ambience {on,off}   quiet waves / wind / birds / city bed per place
  --clip-sound {auto,on,off}
                        use a clip's own sound (real waves, real street) as its ambience when it
                        is clean (default auto)
  --sfx-level DB        effects louder (+3) or quieter (-3)
  --sfx-licenses LIST   Openverse licences to use: cc0,pdm (default, no credit needed) or
                        cc0,pdm,by (credited)

sources (folders are searched recursively, any number of them):
  --exclude GLOB        skip matching files/paths, e.g. --exclude '*/timelapse/*' --exclude
                        'DJI_*.JPG' (repeatable)
  --since YYYY-MM-DD    only media captured on/after this date
  --until YYYY-MM-DD    only media captured on/before this date
  --no-recursive        don't look inside subfolders
  --include-live-photos
                        also use iPhone Live Photo motion clips (skipped by default)
  --watch {auto,gemini,off}
                        Gemini watches each clip (480p proxy, cached): best instant, shake, tilt,
                        whip pans. auto = when GEMINI_API_KEY is set (default)
  --rescore             ask the AI again about these shots instead of reusing its stored verdicts
```

## clone

```text
usage: tripshots clone [-h] [--variants N] [--look LOOK] [--grade-strength 0-1] [--keep-text]
                       [--hype] [--text-preset {bold,editorial,minimal,handwritten,typewriter}]
                       [--upload-copy | --no-upload-copy] [-s STYLE] [-o OUT] [-b BACKEND]
                       [--dry-run] [-j WORKERS] [--cookies-from-browser BROWSER] [--cookies FILE]
                       [--sfx {on,off}] [--ambience {on,off}] [--clip-sound {auto,on,off}]
                       [--sfx-level DB] [--sfx-licenses LIST] [--exclude GLOB]
                       [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--until YYYY-MM-DD] [--no-recursive]
                       [--include-live-photos] [--watch {auto,gemini,off}] [--rescore]
                       [--encoder {auto,hardware,software,videotoolbox,nvenc,qsv}]
                       reference inputs [inputs ...]

positional arguments:
  reference             Instagram reel link (or a saved video) to copy
  inputs                your footage folders/files

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --variants N          N versions using the runner-up shots/text
  --look LOOK           colour: default copies the reference's grade; or auto/none/a look name
  --grade-strength 0-1
  --keep-text           copy the reference's text word for word
  --hype                add the style's freeze-frame / colour-split effects
  --text-preset {bold,editorial,minimal,handwritten,typewriter}
  --upload-copy, --no-upload-copy
                        also write an upload copy without the music (default: on for links)
  -s, --style STYLE     style for motion/text look (default beat-montage)
  -o, --out OUT
  -b, --backend BACKEND
  --dry-run
  -j, --workers WORKERS
  --encoder {auto,hardware,software,videotoolbox,nvenc,qsv}
                        video encoder: auto (default: the Mac's / GPU's hardware encoder when it
                        works, else libx264), hardware, software (libx264, slowest, smallest
                        files), or a specific one

instagram login (most reels need it):
  --cookies-from-browser BROWSER
                        chrome | safari | firefox | brave | edge (use the browser where you're
                        logged in to Instagram; 'chrome:Profile 1' for another profile). Default:
                        $TRIPSHOTS_COOKIES_BROWSER
  --cookies FILE        cookies.txt exported from your browser (alternative)

sound design (real sound effects on the cuts, ambience per place):
  --sfx {on,off}        sound effects on transitions, the drop, text pops (default: style)
  --ambience {on,off}   quiet waves / wind / birds / city bed per place
  --clip-sound {auto,on,off}
                        use a clip's own sound (real waves, real street) as its ambience when it
                        is clean (default auto)
  --sfx-level DB        effects louder (+3) or quieter (-3)
  --sfx-licenses LIST   Openverse licences to use: cc0,pdm (default, no credit needed) or
                        cc0,pdm,by (credited)

sources (folders are searched recursively, any number of them):
  --exclude GLOB        skip matching files/paths, e.g. --exclude '*/timelapse/*' --exclude
                        'DJI_*.JPG' (repeatable)
  --since YYYY-MM-DD    only media captured on/after this date
  --until YYYY-MM-DD    only media captured on/before this date
  --no-recursive        don't look inside subfolders
  --include-live-photos
                        also use iPhone Live Photo motion clips (skipped by default)
  --watch {auto,gemini,off}
                        Gemini watches each clip (480p proxy, cached): best instant, shake, tilt,
                        whip pans. auto = when GEMINI_API_KEY is set (default)
  --rescore             ask the AI again about these shots instead of reusing its stored verdicts
```

## frame

```text
usage: tripshots frame [-h] [-f {post,story,square,both}] [--bg {paper,blur,solid,dark}]
                       [--variant {auto,top,bottom}] [--border] [--look LOOK] [-o OUT]
                       inputs [inputs ...]

positional arguments:
  inputs                photos and/or folders

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -f, --format {post,story,square,both}
                        post = 4:5 feed/carousel, story = 9:16
  --bg {paper,blur,solid,dark}
  --variant {auto,top,bottom}
                        top = head breaks out above the frame, bottom = legs/ground spill below
  --border              white print border around the photo
  --look LOOK           colour grade the photo: auto, a preset or your look (see `tripshots
                        looks`)
  -o, --out OUT         output folder (default ./frames)
```

## find

```text
usage: tripshots find [-h] [--place PLACE] [--near LAT,LON] [--radius RADIUS]
                      [--people NAME [NAME ...]] [--any-people] [--since SINCE] [--until UNTIL]
                      [--kind {both,photo,video}] [--text TEXT] [--only-matching] [--name NAME]
                      [--sheet] [--list]
                      [folders ...]

positional arguments:
  folders               where to look (default: your footage folders, see `tripshots footage`)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --place PLACE         a place name: "Yellowstone National Park", "Lisbon", "Banff"
  --near LAT,LON        instead of a name: around a point
  --radius RADIUS       km around --near (default 10)
  --people NAME [NAME ...]
                        who must be in it: me, mom, ... (see `tripshots people`)
  --any-people          any of --people instead of all of them
  --since SINCE         YYYY-MM-DD
  --until UNTIL         YYYY-MM-DD
  --kind {both,photo,video}
  --text TEXT           words in the folder/file/place name
  --only-matching       don't add same-day files without GPS (default: added, so phone clips come
                        along)
  --name NAME           label for the selection (used in the reel's file name)
  --sheet               also draw a contact sheet of what was found
  --list                also print every file
```

## edits

```text
usage: tripshots edits [-h] [-o OUT] [--no-clips] [--stage | --no-stage] [--picture]
                       [--music {library,file,none}] [--text-as {text,image}] [--url URL]
                       [--token TOKEN] [-j WORKERS]
                       {package,tools,probe,push} [target]

positional arguments:
  {package,tools,probe,push}
                        package: picture + clips + text + audio for Edits; tools: list Edits'
                        automation tools; probe: draft the tool mapping; push: build the timeline
                        in Edits
  target                package: NAME.plan.json; push: the NAME.edits folder

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -o, --out OUT         package: folder to write (default NAME.edits next to the plan)
  --no-clips            package: only the full picture, not one clip per shot
  --stage, --no-stage   package: also copy it where the sandboxed Edits app can open it (default:
                        on a Mac with Edits)
  --picture             push: one video clip instead of one per shot
  --music {library,file,none}
                        push: leave the song to add from Edits' library (default), or add
                        music.m4a
  --text-as {text,image}
                        push: add titles as editable Edits text (default) or as TripShots' styled
                        images
  --url URL             Edits automation server (default $TRIPSHOTS_EDITS_URL or
                        http://127.0.0.1:19501/mcp)
  --token TOKEN         its token (default $TRIPSHOTS_EDITS_TOKEN)
  -j, --workers WORKERS
```

## ask

```text
usage: tripshots ask [-h] [-m MUSIC] [-b {auto,claude-cli,api,minimax}] [--render] [--find-only]
                     [-j WORKERS]
                     request [request ...]

positional arguments:
  request

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -m, --music MUSIC     audio file or reel link (default: the AI picks from TRIPSHOTS_MUSIC)
  -b, --backend {auto,claude-cli,api,minimax}
  --render              render straight away (default: plan + storyboard)
  --find-only           only find the footage (selection + contact sheet)
  -j, --workers WORKERS
```
